content.text:
**Finding: missing (critical) — no IP/ownership article.**

The MSA has no intellectual property or data-ownership provision at all. What exists points the wrong way or is too narrow for AP:

- **p0040** — Kubient warrants it is "the rightful owner or licensee of all intellectual property rights to the Service, the Auction Platform and **products delivered hereunder**," i.e. Kubient owns deliverables, while AP's only licence (**p0002**) is limited, non-transferable, non-sublicensable and **revocable** (and expressly revoked on termination, p0021). No licence-back to anything created for AP.
- **p0025** — makes AP *liable* for the Content and Properties but never confirms AP *owns* them.
- **p0035** — Kubient's handling of visitor data is treated only as a security warranty; there is no purpose limitation and no bar on Kubient selling or monetising AP audience/database data, which is the core value flowing through the Auction Platform (see the "Requests" definition, p0011, and the WHEREAS recital referencing AP's audience and database).
- **p0065** — ownership language covers only names, trademarks and logos.

This fails both the preferred and the fallback position, so I inserted a single new clause 6(b) (validated, `ok:true`): AP retains all right, title and interest in Content, Properties, Inventory, Requests and Customer Data; Kubient retains the Auction Platform and its pre-existing tools and know-how; Kubient assigns deliverables and grants a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to embedded Kubient IP; Kubient may use Customer Data solely to provide the Services and may not monetise it; no joint ownership and no transfer of AP IP.
